title: Shapley-Folkman-Starr Theorem: Large Markets Are Approximately Convex

problemStatement.formal: theorem shapley_folkman_starr [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {ι : Type*} [DecidableEq ι] {S : ι → Set E} {t : Finset ι} (hne : ∀ i ∈ t, (S i).Nonempty) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hdiam : ∀ i ∈ t, ∀ s₁ ∈ S i, ∀ s₂ ∈ S i, dist s₁ s₂ ≤ δ) {x : E} (hx : x ∈ convexHull ℝ (∑ i ∈ t, S i)) : ∃ x' ∈ ∑ i ∈ t, S i, dist x x' ≤ (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ) * δ
problemStatement.plain: For sets {Sᵢ} in a finite-dimensional normed space with pairwise distances bounded by δ, any point x in the convex hull of their Minkowski sum has an approximant x' in the actual sum with ‖x - x'‖ ≤ dim(E)·δ. The bound is independent of the number of summands.
whyMatters: Validates the use of convex analysis in large market equilibrium theory (Starr 1969, Arrow-Hahn 1971)
Per-agent error d·δ/n → 0 as n → ∞: large markets are approximately competitive regardless of individual non-convexities
Foundational for ε-equilibrium theory in mathematical economics
